checked_claims.note: Relative dualizing identification O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C ≅ ω_C ⊗ γ^*O(2) and the packet CE convention W_5 := (O(2) ⊗ γ^*O(-5))|_C correctly yield W_5 ≅ ω_C^{⊗2}(-D) and deg 16, matching SRC-0004 degree arithmetic deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f.
With W_4 ≅ ω_C^{⊗2}, the bundle ω_C ⊗ W_4^vee(Γ) ≅ ω_C^{-1}(Γ) has degree -4 for any degree-6 Γ, so H^0 vanishes universally on smooth curves.

Degree-zero criterion is correct: H^0(ω_C ⊗ W_5^vee(Γ)) ≠ 0 iff O_C(Γ) ≅ ω_C(-D) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{-1}. This discharges the Serre-duality/degree half of the failure condition; the remaining gap is whether these H^0 spaces are exactly the CE evaluation obstruction (asserted, not re-derived from the evaluation map).

Relative P^2-bundle, pure dimension 17, codimension 4 in M_{6,6}, and smoothness of Z^{ord,red} are not established. The proof only uses h^0(D)=2 for general tetragonal curves, never proves constancy of h^0(ω_C(-D)) on the full balanced stack, never produces a rank-3 vector bundle whose projectivization is the relative system, and gives no local criterion for smoothness of the ordered reduced incidence locus. Coarse Hurwitz dimension b-3=15 is used as if it were the stack dimension of the image locus in M_{6,6}.

finding_candidates.evidence: ATT-0022 §3–4 and CLM-Z-DIMENSION explicitly invoke h^0(C,D)=2 only for general tetragonal curves, then conclude a relative P^2 over the full balanced Hurwitz stack and dim Z=15+2=17. Packet subproblem C66-GEO-H0 exists precisely to stratify by h^0, which this attempt never does.
finding_candidates.statement: On the balanced tetragonal stack for (g,n)=(6,6), the identification of the CE evaluation-failure locus with a relative P^2-bundle |ω_C(-D)| (fiber dimension exactly 2) requires proof that h^0(ω_C(-D))=1+h^0(D) is constantly 3 on the whole balanced locus, not merely for general tetragonal curves; without that, pure dimension 17 and codimension 4 in M_{6,6} are not established.

finding_candidates.evidence: ATT-0022 §5 defines Z^{bal,red} by distinct support and asserts the ordered cover is étale Galois with group S_6, then claims the theorem's smooth 17-dimensional stack without any étale-local or deformation-theoretic argument.
finding_candidates.statement: Smoothness of the ordered distinct six-point failure locus Z^{ord,red} as a stack is an independent load-bearing claim: finite étale S_6-covering of a reduced-support open does not yield smoothness unless that open (and the relative linear system) is already smooth, which requires local freeness of the residual system and a smoothness criterion for the incidence of six distinct points.

finding_candidates.evidence: ATT-0022 §4 equates Riemann–Hurwitz branch count b=18 and dim=b-3=15 with the dimension entering codim_{M_{6,6}}(Z)=4, while the theorem statement is stack-theoretic.
finding_candidates.statement: The count dim H_6^{tet,bal}=b-3=15 is a coarse moduli dimension for branched covers modulo Aut(P^1); promoting it to the dimension of a moduli stack of balanced tetragonal curves with marked points, and to codimension inside the stack M_{6,6}, requires a stabilizer/automorphism analysis that ATT-0022 omits.

finding_candidates.evidence: ATT-0022 §2–3 names the H^0 groups as CE obstruction spaces and asserts evaluation drops rank iff the f=5 summand is nonzero after f=4 vanishes, without reconstructing the evaluation map or quoting the lemma beyond matching degree formulas.
finding_candidates.statement: Degree and Serre-duality control of H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_f^vee(Γ)) for f=4,5 is not by itself a complete identification of the Casnati–Ekedahl evaluation-failure locus unless those groups are shown to be exactly the obstruction spaces of the CE evaluation map (packet: derive failure from the f_2=5 summand of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6).

proof_dependency_checks.note: Subproblem has no upstream dependencies, but the attempt does not complete C66-GEO-Z: identification of the failure condition as O(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω^{-1} is essentially in place, while the theorem's pure-dimension, smoothness, relative P^2, and stack-codimension clauses remain undischarged.

strongest_attack: Stack-versus-coarse and h^0-constancy attack on the dimension clause: the theorem requires Z^{ord,red} to be a smooth 17-dimensional stack of codimension 4 in M_{6,6} that is a finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in a relative dimension-2 linear system. The attempt only checks h^0(C,D)=2 for general tetragonal curves (hence h^0(ω_C(-D))=3 only generically), then adds the coarse Hurwitz count dim=b-3=15 and asserts a relative P^2-bundle of total dimension 17. Without constancy of h^0 on the entire balanced tetragonal stack, π_* of the residual system need not be a rank-3 vector bundle, fibers can jump (e.g. whenever the tetragonal pencil is incomplete), the locus need not be pure of dimension 17 or smooth, and the étale S_6-cover statement is only configuration-space reasoning over an unproved smooth base. Smoothness and stack stabilizers are never analyzed. Outcome: CLM-Z-DIMENSION fails; attempt is incomplete for the exact GEO-Z theorem (Pass 1 ends ordinary review).
theorem_statement: Over the moduli stack of genus 6 balanced tetragonal curves with six ordered marked points, the Casnati–Ekedahl evaluation-failure locus $Z$ is canonically isomorphic to the relative incidence scheme of the degree-6 linear system $|W_5 \otimes \omega_C^{-1}| \cong |\omega_C(-D)|$ of dimension 2. Its ordered distinct six-point locus $Z^{\mathrm{ord}, \mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth 17-dimensional stack of codimension 4 in $\mathcal{M}_{6,6}$ that forms a finite étale $\mathfrak{S}_6$-cover of the reduced-support open locus in the relative linear system.
